### 2.1 Consumption, global positivity and F1/F2 — PASS without repairs

Let `Delta_e=y'_e−y_e`, take the original `M≥1` bounding every coordinate of the compact class closure, and retain

`C=max_i K sum_e (−Delta_ei)_+ M^(|y_e|−1)`, `d=max(1,max_e |y_e|)`.

If `Delta_ei<0`, nonnegative integer complexes imply `y_ei≥1`. Thus `x^y_e≤x_i M^(|y_e|−1)`, including source degree one; degree-zero sources cannot contribute to this negative sum. Keeping all positive contributions gives

`x_i' ≥ −C x_i + sum_e (Delta_ei)_+ k_e x^y_e` a.e.

Bounded measurable time coefficients and locally uniform polynomial Lipschitz bounds give unique local Caratheodory solutions. On their positive existence interval, Gronwall gives `x_i(t)≥e^(−C(t−s))x_i(s)`. Stoichiometry keeps the solution in `c+S`; compact closure bounds its speed. At a finite maximal endpoint its limit exists, and the displayed positive floor keeps it in P, where local continuation is available for the same measurable coefficients. Hence the solution is global and strictly positive at each finite time. This proves no eventual floor by itself.

Multiplying the coordinate inequalities, with the exact nonnegative integer exponents, gives `x(u)^y≥e^(−C|y|(u−s))x(s)^y`. On **every** starting window, PE therefore gives original F1:

`integral_s^(s+T) k_e(u)x(u)^y_e du ≥ alpha e^(−CdT)x(s)^y_e`.

Variation of constants in the preceding coordinate inequality has factor `e^(−C(s+T−u))`. Bounding it below by `e^(−CT)`, and the monomial below by `e^(−CdT)x(s)^y_e`, gives precisely original F2:

`x_i(s+T) ≥ e^(−CT)x_i(s)+alpha e^(−C(d+1)T) sum_e (Delta_ei)_+ x(s)^y_e`.

The extra factor is conservative but valid. No product-of-averages identity, differentiable-rate assumption or aligned-window restriction is used.

`A(2)=e b/(1−b+e b)`,

### 2.3 SC, support closure, F3/F4 and binding example — PASS without repairs

Every nonempty siphon contains a minimal siphon, since the species set is finite. A nonnegative conserved vector supported in that minimal siphon also certifies the larger one. Its value `m_Z=w_Z·c` is strictly positive because c is positive and `w_Z` is nonzero. The original finite minimum

`epsilon=min(1,min_Z m_Z/(2||w_Z||_1))`

is therefore positive; the stated convention handles an empty siphon list. If the low-coordinate complement of `J_0={i:x_i(s)≥epsilon}` contained a siphon Z, conservation would give `m_Z<epsilon||w_Z||_1≤m_Z/2`, impossible.

The closure operation uses **all source reactants** of an edge. If a nonempty complement remains at termination, every reaction producing one of those species has a source in the complement, exactly the siphon property. Thus at most n rounds exhaust the species. For a newly added i, `y_ei=0` and `y'_ei≥1`; integer stoichiometry supplies `(Delta_ei)_+≥1`. Since `delta_r≤1` and `|y_e|≤d`, the entire source monomial is at least `delta_r^d`. `delta_(r+1)=min(e^(−CT)delta_r, gamma delta_r^d)`.

Every term is positive and the sequence is nonincreasing; the first entry in the minimum proves monotonicity even if gamma exceeds one. Once the closure is complete, padding a round requires only the old-coordinate term. For any t≥nT, restart this **estimate on the already running trajectory** at s=t−nT. It gives every coordinate at least delta_n at every such t. The resulting closed floor set in the class closure is compact and lies in P. ### 2.4 R1–R3: endpoint orders and exact constants — PASS without repairs

A positive compact-closure rank-one class is an open bounded segment `x(z)=a+vz`, `0<z<L`, with both endpoints on the orthant boundary. At the lower endpoint its zero set Z is nonempty, and positivity for z>0 forces `v_i>0` on Z. Hence `sigma=sum_Z v_i>0`. `p_y'−p_y=c_e sigma`.

Within a linkage class, path sums show any two complexes differ along v. Distinct complexes therefore cannot tie in p. Self-loops contribute zero and are discarded. Isolated complexes and components with only self-loops supply no nonzero vector and do not enter the minimum p. Rank one guarantees a nontrivial component exists. In one achieving the global minimum, weak reversibility gives an edge leaving its minimal complex toward higher p; there is no intervening distinct tied complex. Every decreasing edge, in **any** nontrivial component, has target order at least the same global p and a strictly larger integer source order, hence source order at least p+1.
